identity.name: CYNIC
identity.purpose: Build a sovereign, agentic, OS-like runtime framework from portable low-level primitives.
identity.short_definition: CYNIC is a Rust-first organism runtime: registries declare desired state, host/node/kernel crates observe real state, protocol crates score evidence, and adapters expose bounded commands to humans and agents.

operating_model.rule: Runtime claims start from host, service, network, storage, and kernel read-back; prose cannot promote a layer to healthy.
Every orchestration loop must compare desired state, observed state, and the next safe action.
An agent session is a workload with declared surface, evidence, and validation; it is not an unlimited authority.
CYNIC may use Kubernetes-like semantics, but the domain model must also run on one host, systemd, VMs, LXC, or another substrate.

canonical_layers.responsibility: Schemas, pure planning rules, proof envelopes, KPI scoring, and framework contracts.
Local OS substrate observation and bounded preparation.
Node, mesh, DNS, provider fallback, and network runtime proof.
Persist observations, coordination, runtime proof history, and task memory.
Expose backed capabilities to agents without duplicating domain authority.

primitive_families.role: Declare desired placement, roles, services, and environment-specific topology.
Carry observed runtime evidence between layers without relying on chat or stale files.
Turn desired state and proof bundles into safe read-only, dry-run, and apply boundaries.
Bind portable ports to concrete substrates without leaking provider logic into domain rules.
Give human and LLM agents bounded, inspectable, validation-backed commands.

target_use_cases.description: Run the organism on one machine for development and proof iteration.
Validate N-case topology without binding the framework to one hostname, DNS zone, or provider.
Measure uptime, restart budgets, health latency, proof freshness, and registry/runtime convergence.
Let agents develop safely through explicit surfaces, claims, proofs, validation commands, and next-step scoring.
Provide desired-state reconciliation semantics that can later target Kubernetes, VMs, LXC, systemd, or custom hosts.

agnosticity_rules.rule: Domain types must not require a specific cloud, hypervisor, LLM, browser, DNS zone, or host identity.
A new host, fleet, provider, or deployment model must be represented as registry data or adapter config before code branching.
Systemd, Kubernetes, LXC, SSH, REST, MCP, and shell execution are adapters behind portable ports.

modularity_rules.rule: cynic-protocol owns schemas and pure rules; it must not read the host or mutate runtime state.
cynic-cli wires inputs and outputs; it must not own orchestration semantics.
Host and node crates produce runtime proofs; higher layers consume and persist them.
Add a crate, module, adapter, or contract only when an existing boundary cannot absorb the responsibility cleanly.

non_goals: recreate deleted Python organs as durable authorities
require Kubernetes before single-node execution works
treat LLM session memory as canonical state
centralize all responsibilities in one orchestrator crate
